analysis.investment_thesis: CSSL scores poorly on both Magic Formula metrics — earnings yield of ~8.4% (EBIT ₹31 Cr / EV ~₹371 Cr) falls well short of the 12% threshold, and despite a stated ROCE of 20.4%, consistently negative free cash flow (-₹3, -₹7, -₹26 Cr over three years) signals the returns on capital are illusory. Revenue is growing but the business is burning cash and piling on debt, making it a low-quality compounder at a fair-to-expensive price.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at ~24% CAGR (₹309 Cr → ₹476 Cr), showing real top-line momentum.
Promoter holding of 73% indicates strong owner-operator alignment.
ROCE of 20.4% is nominally above Greenblatt's 20% threshold.
key_risks: Borrowings nearly tripled in two years (₹44 Cr → ₹128 Cr), driving finance costs from ₹4 Cr to ₹10 Cr and squeezing net profit to ₹10 Cr from ₹12 Cr — growth is debt-funded, not self-funded.
Free cash flow is deeply negative and worsening (-₹26 Cr in 2025); OCF positive only 1 of 3 years — the Magic Formula requires real earnings, not accounting profits.
Operating margins are razor-thin at ~6.5% (₹31 Cr EBIT on ₹476 Cr revenue), typical of commoditised facility/security services with no pricing power.
red_flags: Net profit FELL from ₹12 Cr to ₹10 Cr in 2025 despite 37% revenue growth — interest burden is eating the incremental earnings.
Free cash flow of -₹26 Cr in 2025 with financing cash flow of +₹37 Cr: the company is surviving on borrowed money, not operations.
CWIP jumped to ₹22 Cr and total assets doubled to ₹327 Cr — capital is being deployed heavily with no FCF payback visible yet.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the Magic Formula twin tests, CSSL fails to impress. Earnings yield (EBIT ₹31 Cr / EV ~₹371 Cr) comes in at roughly 8.4% — below the 12% floor Greenblatt demands for a stock to even enter the ranking. ROCE of 20.4% is marginally acceptable on paper, but that figure is undermined by the consistently negative free cash flow. The ROIC calculation using capital employed (equity ₹136 Cr + borrowings ₹128 Cr = ₹264 Cr) yields only ~11.7%, squarely in the "mediocre" zone. At a P/E of 18.8x on ₹10 Cr of net profit, the market is paying a full price for a business that converts zero earnings to cash.

The structural story is weak for a Magic Formula investor. Facility management and security staffing are low-moat, labour-intensive businesses with high competitive pressure and no pricing power — exactly the kind Greenblatt screens out in favour of businesses earning high returns on tangible capital. The debt explosion (₹44 Cr → ₹128 Cr in two years), declining net profit, and negative OCF in 2 of 3 years suggest the revenue growth is being funded externally rather than generated organically. Until the business demonstrates self-funding growth with FCF turning positive and margins expanding meaningfully, this fails both halves of the Magic Formula.
